item.title: Vegapay raises $10M in Series A round co-led by Vertex Ventures, Prosus
item.description: Vegapay raises $10 million in a Series A round co-led by Vertex Ventures and Prosus to expand its Credit Line on UPI offerings, launch secured credit products and strengthen its banking technology platform.
item.content:encoded:
Fintech infrastructure startup Vegapay has raised $10 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and Prosus, as it looks to expand its credit infrastructure offerings for banks and financial institutions.

The round also saw participation from existing investors Elevation Capital and Eximius Ventures. It comprised primary and secondary components, with more than 40 employees getting an opportunity to sell a portion of their vested employee stock ownership plans (ESOPs).

Founded in 2022 by Gaurav Mittal, Himanshu Agrawal and Puneet Sharma, Vegapay provides an issuer processing and credit lifecycle management platform for Credit Line on UPI (CLOU) and credit cards.

The company will use the fresh capital to onboard more banks onto its Credit Line on UPI platform, introduce secured credit lines backed by fixed deposits, gold and mutual funds, and expand its credit card, prepaid card and forex card programmes. It also plans to strengthen its engineering and risk teams.

As of November 2026, Vegapay claims to command a majority share of India's Credit Line on UPI market. Its platform is live with YES BANK, Unity Small Finance Bank, Suryoday Small Finance Bank and BOBCARD, and powers programmes for Paytm, BharatPe, Kiwi UPI, Scapia and EbixCash World Money, among others.

Vegapay's platform covers the entire credit lifecycle, including customer onboarding, underwriting, real-time authorisation, billing, repayments and reconciliation. It allows banks to operate multiple co-branded credit programmes on a single platform, with individual credit limits, pricing structures and rules. Banks can deploy the platform on their own cloud infrastructure or on-premises.

“UPI was India’s payments revolution. Credit Line on UPI is the UPI moment for credit, and banks should lead it. At Vegapay, we are building the infrastructure layer that banks need. It runs the full credit line lifecycle for the bank, the bank keeps the customer and the credit book, and one platform can run many co-brand programmes, each with its own limits, pricing and rules,” said Gaurav Mittal, Co-founder and CEO of Vegapay.

Nikhil Marwaha, Partner at Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India, said the adoption of credit on UPI could reshape India's lending landscape, adding that Vegapay's platform enables banks to move from product development to launch within weeks.

Credit Line on UPI allows banks to offer customers pre-sanctioned credit lines that can be used at UPI QR codes through existing payment applications, without requiring a separate card or app. The model is expected to expand access to formal credit by leveraging India's existing digital payments infrastructure.

item.title: Green Aero raises $14M as India pushes for indigenous jet propulsion
item.description: Over the next 12 to 18 months, Green Aero plans to expand engine-testing facilities, hire engineers, and advance the flight qualification of transonic and supersonic drones.
item.content:encoded:
Green Aero, an aerospace and defence startup developing jet engines, military drones and autonomous aircraft, has raised $14 million in a Series A round led by Crane Ventures, an investor focused on artificial intelligence and deeptech.

Other participants were 3one4 Capital, an early-stage venture capital firm, and Antler Elevate, Antler’s growth fund, alongside returning backers pi Ventures, a deeptech investor; Antler India; and Rebalance, an accelerator and angel community.

Over the next 12 to 18 months, Green Aero plans to expand engine-testing facilities, hire engineers, and advance the flight qualification of transonic and supersonic drones. Transonic flight occurs around the speed of sound, while supersonic flight is faster.

The startup also aims to commercialise existing engines, citing early interest from overseas buyers, and bring its drone and combat-aircraft platforms to market. Founder Prithwish Kundu said the funding would accelerate technology development across jet engines, military drones, and collaborative combat aircraft.

Founded in November 2023, Green Aero develops propulsion systems, aircraft electronics, flight-control systems, and airframes in-house. Its 50-member team works from an 87,000 sq ft facility in Bengaluru, which houses research, assembly and testing. Founder Kundu had previously worked at Argonne National Laboratory in the US.

The startup has also developed the Blue Dragon, an aero-engine core built from scratch in India, and completed more than 100 hot-fire tests of its small jet engines. Building on this propulsion work, it is now developing larger-thrust engines alongside autonomous flight-control systems, onboard computing and navigation capabilities designed to operate without satellite signals.

Green Aero's work has received support from Larsen & Toubro, Boeing’s BUILD programme, and SIDBI’s Green-Tech Accelerator.

The startup's technologies are intended to support collaborative combat aircraft, uncrewed military planes designed to operate alongside conventional fighter jets. Air forces are exploring such systems to combine crewed aircraft with autonomous or remotely supervised platforms.

Shubham Sandeep, Partner at pi Ventures, described sovereign propulsion as “a decade-defining opportunity”.

The fundraise comes amid uneven investment in India’s defence-tech sector.

Hyderabad-based Constelli raised $20 million in February 2026 for electronic-warfare and communications systems, while Raphe mPhibr secured $100 million in 2025 to expand its unmanned aircraft business. Tracxn data shows that defence-tech companies raised $73 million through October 2026, compared with $304 million across 61 deals in 2025.

Government support includes iDEX, which had engaged 676 startups, MSMEs and innovators and signed 551 development contracts by March 2026, and ADITI, a companion scheme with a Rs 750 crore outlay. There is also a proposed investment of Rs 5,000 crore programme for an indigenous high-thrust aero-engine.

Edited by Swetha Kannan

item.title: Finnable raises Rs 405 Cr in Series C to expand multi-product lending
item.description: The Bengaluru-based lender has crossed Rs 4,600 crore in assets under management and says it made Rs 51 crore in profit after tax in the first half of FY27.
item.content:encoded:
Fintech company Finnable has raised Rs 405 crore in a Series C round. The new investors are Bharat Value Fund, part of the Pantomath Group, along with Pratithi Investments and NKSquared. Pratithi is the investment vehicle of Infosys co-founder Kris Gopalakrishnan's family, and NKSquared is the firm of Zerodha co-founders Nithin and Nikhil Kamath.

Existing backers Z47, TVS Capital and Claypond Capital continue in the company. TVS Capital and Claypond Capital put in more money in this round. The Rs 405 crore figure carries an asterisk in the company's release. A disclaimer says final allotments and regulatory filings are still being completed and the figure is subject to final subscription numbers.

Profit ahead of last year's full-year total

Finnable said its assets under management crossed Rs 4,600 crore in October 2026. It reported a profit after tax of Rs 51 crore for April to September 2026, which already exceeds the Rs 46 crore it earned in the whole of FY26.

On asset quality, the company said its latest PAR 90 at six months on books stands at 0.24%. This measures loans overdue by more than 90 days among those that have been on the books for six months. Finnable pairs digital loan journeys and technology-led credit assessment with in-house collections.

Three lending lines

Finnable runs three businesses. Its personal loans target salaried professionals, mainly in metros and Tier I cities. Its loan against property (LAP) business offers secured credit to small business owners in Tier II and Tier IV markets. Its consumer finance arm provides instant checkout credit on leading e-commerce platforms, giving it access to younger, digitally active customers.

The company said it combines on-book lending with co-lending partnerships, which co-founder Amit Arora described as a capital-efficient model built to hold up across credit cycles.

Where the money will go

The funds will go towards taking the LAP business into new geographies, scaling consumer finance partnerships and strengthening technology. Finnable also plans to keep investing in AI across underwriting, fraud detection, collections and customer service.

Over the past year the company has also reinforced its board. It has appointed Shrimohan Yadav, a former chief general manager at the Reserve Bank of India, and Sreeram R. Iyer, a former global COO of the corporate and institutional business at ANZ Banking Group. The most recent addition is Sekhar Garisa, managing director at Claypond Capital.

item.title: India, Australia deepen education ties with focus on skills and edtech
item.description: India and Australia are deepening education ties through partnerships in edtech, vocational training and higher education, with a growing emphasis on workforce development and future skills.
item.content:encoded:
Australia is expanding its education relationship with India into joint training, digital learning and workforce development, as a 21-member Australian delegation visits New Delhi and Bengaluru from November 23 to 27. 

Led by the Australian Trade and Investment Commission (Austrade), and supported by Investment NSW and Trade & Investment Queensland, the group is attending DIDAC India 2026 at Bengaluru’s Bangalore International Exhibition Centre from November 25 to 27. 

It includes universities, vocational providers and edtech firms working across schools, employability and workforce development.

Vik Singh, Austrade’s Trade and Investment Commissioner, said the delegation would connect education more closely with economic needs. 

“Through this delegation, we are placing skills development and EdTech at the centre of our collaboration, connecting institutions, industry, governments and learners to build the skills needed for future economic growth. This is about building meaningful partnerships that bring education, technology and workforce needs closer together,” Singh noted.

Eight Australian universities are operating or preparing to establish a presence in India. Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade lists five Australian university branch campuses opened since 2024, in Gujarat’s GIFT City, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Greater Noida. 

Education is Australia’s largest service export to India, valued at A$9.4 billion in 2025, when more than 140,000 Indian students were studying in Australia.

India’s National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 prioritises access, equity, quality and internationalisation in higher education. University Grants Commission rules introduced in 2023 opened the way for eligible foreign universities to establish campuses. 

In December 2025, the bilateral Education and Skills Council backed online and blended learning, dual qualifications and employer-aligned courses, while citing the RMIT-BITS Pilani partnership and Monash University’s teacher-training initiative in Uttar Pradesh.

In July 2026, India’s National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) and Australia’s Australian Skills Quality Authority (ASQA) signed a letter of intent on vocational-training quality assurance, with qualification benchmarking and possible recognition among areas for further exploration. 

The four-year Australia-India Future Skills Initiative supports partnerships for short courses and micro-credentials, short units that certify specific skills, in digital technology, energy, healthcare and infrastructure.

item.title: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down; Lakshmi Venu moves court over family dispute
item.description: Under Krishnamurthy’s leadership, Flipkart grew more than fivefold and strengthened its position in India’s ecommerce market. The company is now preparing for a leadership transition.
item.content:encoded:
Dear Reader, 

Kalyan Krishnamurthy is stepping down as Flipkart CEO after more than 11 years with the company. More on who will lead Flipkart in the interim below.

India’s spacetech ambitions are getting a boost, with Karnataka approving Bengaluru-based Pixxel’s Rs 350 crore proposal to set up a satellite manufacturing facility in the state. The investment further strengthens Bengaluru’s position as a hub for aerospace and advanced manufacturing. 

Meanwhile, AI infrastructure is attracting fresh capital, from data centres to startups that could test their products on live projects. Engineering consultancy Rodic Consultants has proposed a Rs 200 crore fund to back startups developing AI and other technologies for infrastructure, with selected companies getting access to live projects. 

Nexent Capital has also launched a $1 billion fund to invest in AI data centres, quantum-ready infrastructure and advanced energy across India and North America, with a $20 million anchor commitment from the Tyagi family office. 

Early-stage funding is broadening too. US-based VU Venture Partners has launched an accelerator and investment platform in India targeting cheques of $100,000 to $1 million, while Bengaluru-based Aeravti Ventures is targeting Rs 300 crore for its second fund to back 9 to 10 startups across food security, healthcare infrastructure and physical security.

Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs and Societe Generale have acquired a combined stake in eyewear retailer Lenskart for Rs 920.58 crore through block deals, signalling continued investor interest in the company.

  • Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down 
  • Lakshmi Venu files suit seeking partition of family assets

Ecommerce

Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down

Flipkart is preparing for a leadership transition as CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy steps down after more than a decade at the company. Under his leadership, the ecommerce business grew more than fivefold. The company will announce his successor in the coming weeks. 

Key takeaways: 

  • Krishnamurthy is concluding his tenure as CEO after more than 11 years at Flipkart. Balaji Thiagarajan, Chief Product and Technology Officer, and the board will lead the company in the interim, said the company in a statement. 
  • Under Krishnamurthy’s leadership, Flipkart strengthened its position in India’s ecommerce market, expanded its reach across the country, and introduced several innovations for consumers and sellers. The company also established its Big Billion Days sale as a major fixture of India’s festive shopping season.
  • Krishnamurthy said, “It has been a privilege to be part of Flipkart’s journey. I am proud of the scale of the business we have built, but equally proud of how we have built it. Strong ethics, integrity and high standards of governance have been central to Flipkart’s growth.”

News

Lakshmi Venu files suit seeking partition of family assets 

The TVS family’s succession dispute has escalated, with Lakshmi Venu moving the Madras High Court seeking a partition of the joint family assets. She is seeking her claimed share and access to family records. Her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, has backed her claim.

Key takeaways: 

  • Lakshmi Venu has filed a suit seeking partition of the Venu Srinivasan branch’s joint family assets, following a partition notice sent to her father on November 16. 
  • The dispute involves family interests held through the VS Trust and other structures, including stakes in TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services, TVS Holdings and Sundaram-Clayton. 
  • Lakshmi and Mallika Srinivasan maintain that no final economic settlement has been reached. Venu Srinivasan and his son Sudarshan Venu maintain that the family arrangements are consensual, documented and binding.

News & updates

  • AI meets filmmaking: Bengaluru-based EloElo Group has launched Dolphin AI Film Studio, an AI-powered platform designed to help creators turn scripts into video content. Initially developed for the company's internal production needs, the tool has helped its teams create nearly 45,000 videos in six months. The platform currently supports micro-dramas, with plans to expand into films, web series, animation and other formats.  
  • PhonePe IPO: Walmart-backed PhonePe has restarted its IPO plans, targeting a $12-15 billion valuation and a listing in Q1 2027. The proposed $1.2-1.5 billion offering is expected to be an entirely secondary share sale, with Walmart reducing its stake and Tiger Global and Microsoft exiting.

item.title: Capri Global raises $30M in bonds from BlueOrchard Microfinance
item.description: The fundraise will support Capri Global's MSME lending business and expand access to credit for businesses across India.
item.content:encoded:
Capri Global Capital Limited, a retail-focused non-banking financial company (NBFC), has raised $30 million from the BlueOrchard Microfinance Fund, managed by impact investment firm BlueOrchard Finance Ltd.

According to a company statement, this marks Capri Global’s first-ever fundraise from an impact fund. The proceeds will be deployed towards financing activities for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), as well as supporting the company’s growth opportunities.

The fundraising was carried out through a private placement of senior secured, US dollar-denominated bonds with a tenor of 36 months and a maturity date in November 2029. BlueOrchard was the sole investor in the issuance, and the bonds will be listed on NSE IFSC Limited.

“India’s MSME sector has significant potential to drive economic growth, entrepreneurship and employment. Realising this potential will require a stronger credit ecosystem that can meet the diverse financing needs of businesses at every stage of their growth. Institutional capital and long-term partnerships will be key to this effort. Our partnership with BlueOrchard strengthens our ability to deepen our reach in the MSME segment and support a more inclusive credit landscape,” said Rajesh Sharma, Managing Director, Capri Global Capital.

Capri Global said this fundraise further diversifies its liability profile demonstrating the ability to access a broad range of domestic and international funding sources.

Alongside development and impact-focused investors, the company’s funding sources include domestic banks and financial institutions, domestic bond issuances, co-lending arrangements, direct assignment transactions and international capital market programmes.

“For impact investing to deliver meaningful outcomes, capital must be channelled through institutions with the ability to reach businesses that are critical to local economies. Our investment in Capri Global reflects our approach of partnering with financial institutions to support the flow of capital to this segment, while contributing to broader economic resilience and sustainable growth,” said Normunds Mizis, Chief Credit Officer, BlueOrchard Finance.
